newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end flat, small-caps highlighted.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end flat, small-caps highlighted.

text.p: Stocks closed a fraction firmer as lethargic blue chip performance limited the index rise, otherwise inspired by strong buying interest among individual small-capitalised shares, brokers said on Wednesday.
The composite stock index rose 0.35 points to provisionally end at 782.11. But the small-cap sub-index gained 14.50 points to 1,972.79.

"While many sold small-caps for quick profit, others bought because they felt there were no other good alternatives," said Kwon Oh-seung of Samsung Securities. "It looks unlikely they will sustain the recent steep rises."
Many of 118 stocks to go limit up were small-cap shares, brokers said. Small-caps represented nearly 80 percent of today's trading volume of 28.96 million shares.

Of those in the spotlight, Seondo Electric closed at a year high of 124,500 won, rising 7,000 won. Jaeil Engineering hit daily upper limit of 20,300 won, up 1,100, as it hit today's largest volume with 685,790 shares. Daesung Resources climbed 8,500 won to its daily permittable high level of 154,500 won.
But Kang Chang-joo of Ssangyong Securities warned : "Nobody knows when the small-cap rally will suddenly stop."
"Without gains in the large-caps, the market is not expected to turn around," Kang said. "Selling from margin accounts will decide the future market direction."
LG Electronics, a major shareholder in LG Semicon, which is holding its IPO on Wednesday and Thursday, fell 400 won to 13,900 on profit taking.
Brokers said investors shrugged off the news that a group of possibly 10 North Korean infiltrators landed on a South Korean beach in a small submarine.
The bourse later revised the closing index to 782.10.
